messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: 5xx spike detected for service 'inference-edge' behind ELB tg-inference-usw2b (us-west-2b). 90s sustained error rate > 12%.
amy: i'm on it. grabbing logs and healthchecks now.
rob: seeing ELB healthcheck failures from ~08:12 UTC. target status: Unhealthy -> draining.
jessie: any recent deploys to that ASG?
amy: not from deploy bot. last deploy 07:45 UTC, different ASG.
mike: tracing the failures — connections reset on accept, backlog full. sample tcpdump shows RSTs coming from instance ENI, not upstream.
amy: can someone run a quick healthcheck against a healthy instance vs unhealthy? curl -v http://10.2.34.56:8080/health
rob: healthy instance returns 200 within 40ms. unhealthy returns 504 from ELB then RST on socket.
jessie: EBS attach/detach events in cloudtrail for that AZ at 08:10-08:14. a few nodes had volumes re-attached. could be IO stalls.
amy: that matches paged alerts about EBS IO stalls in us-west-2b. AWS status shows a Partial AZ networking/ebs event. linking: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — note: us-west-2b EBS IO & ENI flap entry.
kai: customer impact? which traffic flows hit that AZ specifically?
amy: per traffic split, ~18% of prod requests go to us-west-2b (weighted LB across AZs). of that, ~70% routed to tg-inference-usw2b -> so ~12% of global requests seeing 5xx.
mike: can we quick-shift Route53 weights to avoid us-west-2b? TTL is 30s on the weighted record. we can temporarily reduce weight to 0 and push to other AZs/region failover.
amy: agree. plan: 1) set Route53 weighted record for inference.edge -> set weight(usw2b)=0, weight(usw2a)=+, weight(usw2c)=+. 2) drain targets in tg-inference-usw2b. 3) open high-priority AWS support case for EBS/ENI. 4) monitor error rate, revert when stable.
rob: i'm bumping capacity in other AZs: scaling policy triggered to +15 instances in us-west-2a/2c.
jessie: adding nginx-level circuit breaker to reduce retries to backend to reduce error amplification.
pd-bot: Paging oncall-sre (amy) acknowledged at 08:19 UTC. Escalation to infra-eng (rob) at 08:25 UTC.
amy: executing route53 change now. command: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"usw2b","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.12.34.56"}]}}]}'
```
rob: change submitted. propagation expected < 30s.
mike: watching ELB metrics — 5xx rate dropping in ~40s, healthy host count in tg-inference-usw2b goes to 0 as we drain. global error rate dropped from 12% -> 2.3%.
kai: update for customers: "We observed partial service degradation in US-WEST-2 for a subset of endpoints. Traffic has been shifted away from the affected AZ and error rates have reduced. We're investigating root cause with the provider."
jessie: creating incident channel #incident-3701123456 and assigning postmortem owner.
amy: created ASG drain and marked instances for investigation. collecting dmesg/kernel logs + EBS error logs from drained hosts.
rob: AWS case opened (Case 987654321): EBS IO exception + ENI flap in us-west-2b. AWS engineering engaged.
mike: note: some customers behind sticky session cookies may have continued failing for a short window due to DNS caching at CDN edges. we've flagged the CDN to purge minimal objects and lower TTLs.
amsg: (typo notice) sorry — meant amy.
amy: no worries. current status: mitigation in place, traffic shifted, metrics stabilizing. next: restore instances only after AWS confirms EBS/ENI health and we validate IO latency < 10ms for 10m.
kai: customer impact assessment (initial): affected requests ~12% of global for 18 minutes. Estimated error budget burn: high for that window; approx 1.2% user-visible outage overall. list of impacted customers being built by support.
jessie: logging thread for postmortem: root cause hypotheses: EBS IO stall causing kernel-level networking hang -> ENI resets -> ELB healthcheck failures. alternative: underlying AZ network fabric causing both EBS and ENI errors.
amy: leaving handoff to night oncall (mike) at 09:00 UTC. mike, you have the runbook + aws case id.
mike: got it. i'll monitor and hold until AWS confirms healthy. will re-enable weight for usw2b only after 30m stable healthy hosts and no EBS detach events.
incident-bot: Incident 3701123456 -> mitigated (traffic shifted). severity: Sev2. Logs and timeline will be attached to incident postmortem.
rob: filing short RCA draft. assigning to jessie for timeline, amy for mitigation notes.
amy: thanks all. will post updates to #status-updates and kick off postmortem template after wrap.
mike: quick note: customers behind dedicated dedicated-natgw in that AZ may need explicit reattach. support, pls coordinate.
kai: support is on it, contacting top 10 affected customers with mitigation summary.
rob: closing thread for live mitigation; moving discussion to #incident-3701123456-rca for postmortem work.
incident-bot: Reminder: postmortem due in 72 hours.
